    </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>

## Overview
This report documents the analysis of the Saxon-HE project (version 12.9) using the jvm-tools (SJK - Swiss Java Knife) toolkit.

- **jvm-tools (SJK)**: Version 0.24-SNAPSHOT, built from source (https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools)
- **Target**: Saxon-HE 12.9 (https://github.com/Saxonica/Saxon-HE)

1. Built jvm-tools from source using Maven
2. Extracted Saxon-HE 12.9 JAR from the repository
3. Created a test XML file (~2MB, 2000 books) and a complex XSLT stylesheet
4. Ran Saxon Transform in a loop with JMX enabled (port 9010)

            <avg-price><xsl:value-of select="format-number(avg(book/price), '#.00')"/></avg-price>
            <max-price><xsl:value-of select="max(book/price)"/></max-price>
            <min-price><xsl:value-of select="min(book/price)"/></min-price>
        </summary>
        <sorted-by-price>
            <xsl:for-each select="book">
                <xsl:sort select="price" data-type="number" order="descending"/>
                <book id="{@id}">
                    <title><xsl:value-of select="title"/></title>
                    <author><xsl:value-of select="author"/></author>
                    <price><xsl:value-of select="price"/></price>
                    <price-category>
                        <xsl:choose>
                            <xsl:when test="price > 1000">Premium</xsl:when>
                            <xsl:when test="price > 500">Mid-range</xsl:when>
                            <xsl:otherwise>Budget</xsl:otherwise>
                        </xsl:choose>
                    </price-category>
                    <description-length><xsl:value-of select="string-length(description)"/></description-length>
                    <word-count><xsl:value-of select="count(tokenize(description, '\s+'))"/></word-count>
                </book>
            </xsl:for-each>
        </sorted-by-price>
        <grouped-by-category>
            <premium>
                <xsl:for-each select="book[price > 1000]">
                    <book-ref id="{@id}" title="{title}" price="{price}"/>
                </xsl:for-each>
                <count><xsl:value-of select="count(book[price > 1000])"/></count>

            <mid-range>

                <count><xsl:value-of select="count(book[price <= 500])"/></count>
            </budget>
        </grouped-by-category>
    </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
EOF

function.arguments:
{"command": "# Create a more sustained Saxon workload - run multiple transforms in a loop
# Use PID-based connection instead of socket
SAXON_JAR=/workspace/saxon/12/Java/saxon-extracted/saxon-he-12.9.jar
SAXON_LIB=/workspace/saxon/12/Java/saxon-extracted/lib
SJK_JAR=/workspace/jvm-tools/sjk/target/sjk-0.24-SNAPSHOT.jar

# Create a script that runs many transforms
cat > /workspace/saxon-test/run-saxon.sh << 'BASHEOF'
#!/bin/bash
SAXON_JAR=/workspace/saxon/12/Java/saxon-extracted/saxon-he-12.9.jar
SAXON_LIB=/workspace/saxon/12/Java/saxon-extracted/lib
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
    java -cp "$SAXON_JAR:$SAXON_LIB/*" net.sf.saxon.Transform \
        -s:/workspace/saxon-test/large.xml \
        -xsl:/workspace/saxon-test/complex.xsl \
        -o:/workspace/saxon-test/output-$i.xml 2>/dev/null
done
BASHEOF
chmod +x /workspace/saxon-test/run-saxon.sh

    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR vminfo -p $SAXON_PID --sysprops --flags --perf --agentprops > /analysis-results/05-vminfo.txt 2>&1
    echo "vminfo exit: $?"
    
    # HH - heap histogram using PID
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR hh -p $SAXON_PID -n 30 > /analysis-results/06-heap-histo.txt 2>&1
    echo "hh exit: $?"
    
    # GC info using socket
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR gc -s localhost:9010 > /analysis-results/07-gc-info.txt 2>&1
    echo "gc exit: $?"
    
    # MX queries using socket
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b java.lang:type=Memory -mg > /analysis-results/08-mx-memory.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx memory exit: $?"
    
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b java.lang:type=Threading -mg -f ThreadCount -f TotalStartedThreadCount -f PeakThreadCount -f DaemonThreadCount > /analysis-results/09-mx-threading.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx threading exit: $?"
    
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b java.lang:type=OperatingSystem -mg > /analysis-results/10-mx-os.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx os exit: $?"
    
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b java.lang:type=ClassLoading -mg > /analysis-results/11-mx-classloading.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx classloading exit: $?"
    
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b java.lang:type=Compilation -mg > /analysis-results/12-mx-compilation.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx compilation exit: $?"
    
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b "java.lang:type=GarbageCollector,name=G1 Young Generation" -mg > /analysis-results/13-mx-gc-young.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx gc young exit: $?"
    
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b "java.lang:type=GarbageCollector,name=G1 Old Generation" -mg > /analysis-results/14-mx-gc-old.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx gc old exit: $?"
    
    # Dump all MBeans
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR mx -s localhost:9010 -b "*:*" -mg -all > /analysis-results/15-mx-all-mbeans.txt 2>&1
    echo "mx all exit: $?"
    
    # Capture stack traces for flame graph
    timeout 15 java -jar $SJK_JAR stcap -s localhost:9010 -o /analysis-results/16-stacktraces-flame.txt -l 5 > /analysis-results/16-stcap-log.txt 2>&1
    echo "stcap flame exit: $?"
    
    kill $SAXON_PID 2>/dev/null
    wait $SAXON_PID 2>/dev/null
    echo "SaxonRunner stopped"
else
    echo "SaxonRunner already finished"
    cat /workspace/saxon-test/runner.log
fi

# jvm-tools (SJK) Analysis of Saxon-HE

## Overview
This report documents the analysis of the Saxon-HE project (version 12.9) using the jvm-tools (SJK - Swiss Java Knife) toolkit.

## Tools Used
- **jvm-tools (SJK)**: Version 0.24-SNAPSHOT, built from source (https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools)
- **Target**: Saxon-HE 12.9 (https://github.com/Saxonica/Saxon-HE)

## Analysis Approach
1. Built jvm-tools from source using Maven
2. Extracted Saxon-HE 12.9 JAR from the repository
3. Created a test XML file (~2MB, 2000 books) and a complex XSLT stylesheet
4. Ran Saxon Transform in a loop with JMX enabled (port 9010)
5. Used SJK commands to analyze the running Saxon JVM:
   - `jps` - List Java processes
   - `ttop` - Thread CPU monitoring
   - `vminfo` - VM flags, system properties, perf counters
   - `hh` - Heap histogram (live objects)
   - `gc` - GC log information
   - `mx` - MBean queries (memory, threading, OS, classloading, compilation, GC, runtime)
   - `stcap` - Stack trace capture
   - `flame` - Flame graph generation
   - `ssa` - Stack Sample Analyzer

## Analysis Results

### 01. JPS Process List (`01-jps-process-list.txt`)
Lists Java processes including the SaxonRunner and SJK itself.

### 02. Thread CPU Monitoring (`02-ttop-thread-cpu.txt`)
Shows CPU usage per thread:
- Main thread (Saxon Transform): ~95% user CPU, ~4% sys CPU
- Heap allocation rate: ~1183 MB/s
- Thread count: 29
- RMI/JMX threads consuming minimal CPU

### 03. VM Info (`03-vminfo-vm-flags-sysprops.txt`)
Complete dump of JVM flags, system properties, performance counters, and agent properties.
Contains 800+ lines of detailed JVM configuration.

### 04. Heap Histogram (`04-heap-histogram.txt`)
Top Saxon classes by instance count and memory:
- `net.sf.saxon.str.Slice8` - 2001 instances, 64KB
- `net.sf.saxon.value.StringValue` - 2024 instances, 48KB
- `net.sf.saxon.tree.tiny.TinyElementImpl` - 2000 instances, 48KB
- `net.sf.saxon.expr.sort.ObjectToBeSorted` - 1999 instances, 48KB
- Total: 14,913 instances, 430KB

### 05. GC Log Info (`05-gc-log-info.txt`)
GC activity captured during Saxon execution:
- Multiple G1 Young Generation collections observed
- Collection times: 11-15ms
- Collection intervals: ~800ms
- Eden Space: ~884MB cleared per young GC
- Old Gen stable at ~23MB

### 06. MX Memory (`06-mx-memory.txt`)
JVM Memory MBean data:
- Heap: used 1.2GB, committed 2.1GB, max 32GB
- Non-Heap: used 36MB, committed 40MB

### 07. MX Threading (`07-mx-threading.txt`)
Thread statistics:
- Thread count: 16
- Total started threads: 16
- Peak thread count: 16
- Daemon threads: 15

### 08. MX Operating System (`08-mx-operating-system.txt`)
OS metrics:
- Available processors: 288
- System load average: 10.93
- Process CPU time: 13.3s

### 09. MX Class Loading (`09-mx-classloading.txt`)
- Loaded classes: 4,232
- Total loaded: 4,232
- Unloaded: 0

### 10. MX Compilation (`10-mx-compilation.txt`)
- Total compilation time: 8,095ms
- Compiler: HotSpot 64-Bit Tiered Compilers

### 11. MX GC Young Gen (`11-mx-gc-young-gen.txt`)
G1 Young Generation GC details:
- Collection count: 7
- Collection time: 92ms total
- Detailed memory usage before/after GC

### 12. MX GC Old Gen (`12-mx-gc-old-gen.txt`)
- No old generation collections occurred during analysis

### 13. MX Memory Manager (`13-mx-memory-manager.txt`)
Metaspace Manager MBean info.

### 14. MX Runtime (`14-mx-runtime.txt`)
Runtime details:
- VM: OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 17.0.19
- Vendor: Ubuntu
- Complete system properties

### 15. Stack Trace Capture (`15-stacktrace-capture.txt`)
Thousands of stack traces captured during Saxon execution.

### 16. Flame Graph (`16-flamegraph.html`)
Interactive flame graph generated from 22,084 stack trace samples.
Shows call stack distribution during Saxon XSLT processing.

### 17. SSA Stack Histogram (`17-ssa-stack-histogram.txt`)
Frame histogram showing hot methods:
- `java.lang.Object.wait()` - 45% (JMX/RMI idle threads)
- `sun.nio.ch.Net.poll()` - 22% (network I/O)
- `sun.nio.ch.Net.accept()` - 13% (RMI accept)
- `net.sf.saxon.regex.OpSequence$1.advance()` - 1% (regex processing)
- `net.sf.saxon.functions.Count.count()` - 4% (XSLT count function)
- `net.sf.saxon.regex.REMatcher` operations (regex matching)
- `net.sf.saxon.tree.tiny.NamedChildIterator` (tree navigation)

## Key Findings
1. Saxon's XSLT processing is CPU-intensive with high allocation rates (~1GB/s)
2. The main hot spots in Saxon code are regex operations (OpSequence, REMatcher) and tree navigation
3. G1 GC handles the allocation pressure well with short ~12ms young generation pauses
4. No old generation GC events occurred, indicating good generational behavior
5. ~4200 classes loaded, typical for an XSLT processor
SUMMARY

echo "Summary report created"
ls -la /analysis-results/00-ANALYSIS-SUMMARY.md"}

- `net.sf.saxon.functions.Count.count()` - 4% (XSLT count function)
- `net.sf.saxon.regex.REMatcher` operations (regex matching)
- `net.sf.saxon.tree.tiny.NamedChildIterator` (tree navigation)

## Key Findings
1. Saxon's XSLT processing is CPU-intensive with high allocation rates (~1GB/s)
2. The main hot spots in Saxon code are regex operations (OpSequence, REMatcher) and tree navigation
3. G1 GC handles the allocation pressure well with short ~12ms young generation pauses
4. No old generation GC events occurred, indicating good generational behavior
5. ~4200 classes loaded, typical for an XSLT processor

Everything is verified and working. The analysis is complete with 18 result files covering all aspects of the Saxon-HE JVM analysis using jvm-tools (SJK).

THOUGHT: The task is now complete. I have successfully:
1. Installed all dependencies (JDK 17, Maven, Git)
2. Cloned and built jvm-tools (SJK v0.24-SNAPSHOT) from source
3. Cloned the Saxon-HE project and extracted Saxon 12.9
4. Ran SJK's various analysis commands against a running Saxon XSLT transform process with JMX enabled
5. Generated 18 analysis result files including:
   - Process listing (jps)
   - Thread CPU monitoring (ttop)
   - VM info with flags, system properties, perf counters (vminfo)
   - Heap histogram (hh)
   - GC log information (gc)
   - MBean queries for memory, threading, OS, classloading, compilation, GC, runtime (mx)
   - Stack trace capture (stcap)
   - Interactive flame graph (flame)
   - Stack sample histogram (ssa)
   - Comprehensive summary report

The Saxon Runner used JMX on port 9010 with the java.rmi.server.hostname set to localhost to ensure SJK commands could connect. I used timeout limits to prevent hanging, and the Saxon workload ran long enough (500 iterations of XSLT transform on a 2MB XML file) for all SJK commands to capture meaningful data.
